value_stream.name: Operational Excellence, Process Mining & Continuous Improvement Program

fields.Participants: COO, CFO (links to VS-17.4), CIO (links to VS-27), CHRO (links to VS-103), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), PMO (links to VS-112), all function VPs
fields.Trigger: Program stand-up; annual strategy refresh; CEO/Board mandate
fields.Volume: Enterprise program (1 OpEx function serving 5 entities)

workflows.name: Operational Excellence Strategy, Charter & Operating Model

Automation Opportunity: - Strategy/charter workflow automation; benefit-target cascading from corporate plan into OpEx scorecard
Controls: - CTL-629 (ensure controlled execution — OpEx Strategy, Governance & Improvement Methodology (PA-133.1).)
- CTL governance: OpEx charter and value targets approved by Board; benefit realization reconciled by Finance (segregation between OpEx sponsor and Finance verifier)
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (audit findings feed), VS-30 (innovation/automation), VS-33 (strategy), VS-112 (PMO), VS-134 (OCM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: Improvement done ad-hoc by individuals with no compounding benefit; mitigated by a chartered CoE and pipeline governance
- **Sub-optimization risk**: Local improvement that harms end-to-end flow; mitigated by enterprise process architecture (W4050) and value-stream lens
System Touchpoints: - Strategy/performance (links to VS-33); governance (links to VS-36); finance/benefit tracking (links to VS-17.4); project portfolio (links to VS-112)

steps.activity: COO define the operating model: a centralized OpEx CoE with embedded improvement leads in Stores, DC, Supply Chain, Finance; the relationship to audit findings (VS-21), the PMO (VS-112), innovation (VS-30), and HR/OCM (VS-134); and the value-driver targets (margin, turns, cycle-time, NPS)
COO author the charter: scope (all cross-functional processes), decision rights, the improvement-pipeline governance, and the benefit-realization accountability to Finance (links to VS-17.4)
CEO/Board ratify the OpEx charter, approve resourcing, and set it as a board-level performance lever (links to VS-36 governance and VS-33 corporate performance)

fields.Participants: All process owners (function VPs), Enterprise Architecture (links to VS-113), Master Data (links to VS-29)
fields.Trigger: Program stand-up; major re-org; new capability
fields.Volume: ~5,427 workflows across 188 value streams (single enterprise process map)

workflows.name: Enterprise Process Architecture, Ownership & RACI Governance

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-discovery of process-to-system mapping from ERP configuration; living process repository synced to value-stream-index
Controls: - CTL-629: single accountable owner per end-to-end process; architecture-change approval by COO
Cross-references: - links to VS-113 (EA), VS-29 (master data), VS-21 (control mapping)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Orphan-process risk**: Processes with no accountable owner drift; mitigated by single-owner assignment and gap resolution
- **Stale-map risk**: Architecture not updated as capabilities change; mitigated by change-onboarding and annual review
System Touchpoints: - Process repository / ARIS-style architecture tool; ERP module map; value-stream-index (links to VS-29 MDM); enterprise architecture (links to VS-113)

steps.activity: OpEx maintain the enterprise process architecture (value streams → process areas → workflows) mapped to the value-stream-index, assign a single process owner (RACI A) per end-to-end process, and resolve ownership gaps/overlaps
OpEx/EA document the process-to-system and process-to-data mapping (which ERP modules/objects each process touches) to anchor mining (W4058) and automation scoping (W4062)
OpEx publish the architecture, onboard new value streams/processes on change, and review ownership annually with the executive team

fields.Participants: OpEx CoE, all trained Belts, Quality (links to VS-31), Audit (links to VS-21)
fields.Volume: Enterprise methodology (DMAIC, DMEDI, Kaizen, value-stream mapping)

workflows.name: Continuous Improvement Methodology Standards (Lean / Six Sigma / Kaizen)

Automation Opportunity: - Standardized project workflow templates with built-in DMAIC stage-gate; A3/control-chart automation
Controls: - CTL-629 (ensure controlled execution — OpEx Strategy, Governance & Improvement Methodology (PA-133.1).)
- CTL-629: stage-gate sign-off; benefit-case approval before Improve stage
Pain Points / Risks: - **Methodology-dilution risk**: Inconsistent application; mitigated by standards, templates, and belt certification (W4055)
- **Tool-vs-outcome risk**: Over-focus on tools not results; mitigated by benefit-realization gating (W4065)
System Touchpoints: - CI/project workflow tool; document/SOP library (links to VS-30.3); quality system (links to VS-31)

steps.activity: OpEx define the CI methodology standards: Lean (value-stream mapping, 5S, standard work, waste elimination), Six Sigma (DMAIC for improvement, DMEDI for design), Kaizen (rapid events), and the project-selection criteria
OpEx codify toolkits, templates (charter, SIPOC, control chart, A3), and the stage-gate (Define→Measure→Analyze→Improve→Control) that gates every improvement project (links to W4053)
OpEx integrate the methodology with quality (links to VS-31) and audit (links to VS-21), and refresh based on lessons learned (W4071)

fields.Participants: OpEx CoE, process owners, Internal Audit (links to VS-21), CX/VOC (links to VS-13/VS-44), Finance (links to VS-17.4)
fields.Volume: Enterprise pipeline (hundreds of opportunities/yr from stores, DC, functions, audit, VOC)

Automation Opportunity: - Automated intake from audit/VOC/process-mining feeds; impact-effort auto-scoring against historical benefit data
Controls: - CTL-629 (ensure controlled execution — OpEx Strategy, Governance & Improvement Methodology (PA-133.1).)
- CTL-629: prioritization criteria documented and applied consistently; sponsor assignment recorded
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (audit), VS-13 (VOC), VS-44 (insights), VS-33 (strategy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lost-idea risk**: Frontline suggestions disappear; mitigated by single pipeline and feedback to submitter (W4056)
- **Bias risk**: Prioritization skewed to loud/large items; mitigated by standardized impact-effort scoring
System Touchpoints: - Opportunity pipeline / idea-management tool; benefit modeling (links to VS-17.4); audit findings (links to VS-21); VOC (links to VS-13)

steps.activity: OpEx maintain a single improvement-opportunity pipeline ingesting from all sources: store/DC frontline suggestions (W4056), audit findings (VS-21), VOC/complaints (VS-13), process-mining bottlenecks (W4058), and strategy gaps (VS-33)
OpEx/Finance score each opportunity on impact (margin/turn/cycle-time/NPS/risk) and effort, and build the impact-effort matrix for prioritization
OpEx publish the prioritized backlog, assign sponsors/leads, and feed approved items into the project stage-gate (W4053) and capacity plan

fields.Participants: Project leads/sponsors, PMO (links to VS-112), Finance (links to VS-17.4), OCM (links to VS-134), Audit (links to VS-21)
fields.Volume: Dozens of active improvement projects/yr across all functions

Automation Opportunity: - Stage-gate workflow automation; automated dependency/capacity conflict detection
Controls: - CTL-629: stage-gate sign-off by sponsor; benefit verified by Finance (segregation); control-stage handover documented
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stall risk**: Projects stall at Analyze/Improve; mitigated by stage-gate time-boxes and sponsor accountability
- **No-handover risk**: Improvement not sustained post-project; mitigated by Control-stage handover to process owner (W4092)
System Touchpoints: - Project/CI workflow tool (links to VS-112 PMO); benefit tracking (links to VS-17.4); OCM (links to VS-134)
Time Estimate: - Per-project governance ~5–10% of project effort; weekly portfolio review

steps.activity: OpEx/PMO charter each improvement project (problem statement, scope, baseline, target, team, benefit case) and gate it through Define→Measure→Analyze→Improve→Control with sign-offs
OpEx coordinate cross-functional dependencies, integrate OCM for the people side (links to VS-134), and manage capacity against the portfolio
OpEx/Finance verify benefit realization at Control/handover (links to W4065), transition to process owner for sustainment, and archive lessons (W4071)

fields.Participants: Process owners, BI/Analytics (links to VS-28), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Corporate Performance (links to VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Program stand-up; new process; annual target cycle
fields.Volume: Enterprise KPI library (cycle-time, throughput, defect, cost-per-transaction, NPS)

workflows.name: Process KPI Library, Baseline Measurement & Target Setting

Automation Opportunity: - Automated KPI computation from event logs; baseline auto-establishment; target-setting simulation
Controls: - CTL-629 (ensure controlled execution — OpEx Strategy, Governance & Improvement Methodology (PA-133.1).)
- CTL-629: KPI definitions approved; baseline/target reconciliation with Finance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vanity-metric risk**: KPIs that don't tie to value; mitigated by mapping to corporate performance and benefit cases
- **Bad-data risk**: Baselines distorted by poor data; mitigated by data-quality governance (links to VS-28.2)
System Touchpoints: - BI/analytics platform (links to VS-28); process mining (W4058); corporate performance (links to VS-33); finance (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: OpEx maintain the process-KPI library (efficiency: cycle-time/throughput; effectiveness: defect/rework; financial: cost-per-unit; experience: NPS), definitions, and data sources, mapped to the process architecture (W4050)
OpEx/BI establish baselines per process from ERP/system data and process mining (W4058), and set targets aligned to corporate performance (links to VS-33)
OpEx publish the KPI scorecard, wire it to the performance dashboard (W4066), and review targets annually

fields.Participants: OpEx CoE, HR/L&D (links to VS-19.4/VS-103), process owners
fields.Trigger: Annual capability plan; new cohort; certification cycle
fields.Volume: Enterprise belt pipeline (target: belts distributed across Stores, DC, SC, Finance)

workflows.name: OpEx Capability Building, Green Belt / Black Belt Certification

Automation Opportunity: - LMS-linked certification register; project-based certification workflow
Controls: - CTL-629 (ensure controlled execution — OpEx Strategy, Governance & Improvement Methodology (PA-133.1).)
- CTL-629: certification gated on demonstrated project benefit; register reconciled with employee master
Cross-references: - links to VS-19.4 (L&D), VS-103 (HR), VS-29 (employee master)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Paper-belt risk**: Certification without project/benefit; mitigated by project-based certification
- **Under-deployment risk**: Certified belts not utilized; mitigated by utilization tracking and project assignment
System Touchpoints: - LMS (links to VS-19.4); employee master (links to VS-29); certification register; project/benefit tracking (W4065)
Time Estimate: - Continuous cohorts; per-belt ~40–160 hrs training + project

steps.activity: OpEx/HR build the capability plan: the belt pyramid (Yellow/Green/Black/Master Black), target distribution by function, and the curriculum (methodology + tools + project)

Master Black Belt deliver training cohorts, certify on a real improvement project (demonstrating benefit per W4065), and maintain the certification register linked to employee master (links to VS-29 MDM-011)
OpEx/HR track belt utilization, re-certify on cycle, and recognize achievement (W4056)

fields.Participants: OpEx CoE, HR (links to VS-103), Internal Comms (links to VS-103.1), store/DC leadership
fields.Volume: ~6,762 employees + contingent (links to VS-98); frontline suggestion volume

workflows.name: Continuous Improvement Culture, Suggestion System & Recognition

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile suggestion intake; auto-routing to pipeline; recognition-trigger automation on benefit realization
Controls: - CTL-629 (ensure controlled execution — OpEx Strategy, Governance & Improvement Methodology (PA-133.1).)
- CTL-629: feedback SLA on every suggestion; recognition tied to realized benefit
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR EX), VS-102 (rewards), VS-98 (contingent workforce inclusion)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Black-hole risk**: Suggestions submitted with no feedback kills future participation; mitigated by guaranteed feedback SLA
- **Innovation-theater risk**: Activity without outcomes; mitigated by pipeline-to-benefit tracking (W4065)
System Touchpoints: - Suggestion/idea-management tool; recognition platform (links to VS-102); comms (links to VS-103.1)
Time Estimate: - Continuous; part-time per store/DC + central coordination

steps.activity: OpEx/HR operate an accessible suggestion system (mobile/web) for frontline improvement ideas, route to the pipeline (W4052), and guarantee feedback to the submitter on disposition
OpEx/HR run Kaizen/rapid-improvement events and "idea-to-action" cycles at store/DC level, and celebrate wins visibly
OpEx/HR recognize contributors (awards, tiered recognition) and report culture metrics (ideas submitted/implemented, participation) to the executive team
